time_hour, carrier, flight, origin and sched_dep_time are all null_rate 0.0 and together describe one scheduled departure leg; carrier has 16 distinct values, origin 3, flight 2994 and time_hour 3439, none unique alone, so the composite is the smallest defensible grain and a reviewer must measure its uniqueness against the warehouse.

Every numeric column lands as DECIMAL(38,9) but all reported min/max and sample_values are integral (for example distance min 80.0 max 4983.0, minute min 0.0 max 59.0), so each is cast to INTEGER.

dep_time, sched_dep_time, arr_time and sched_arr_time range between 1.0 and 2400.0, an HHMM clock encoding rather than a duration; they are kept as INTEGER because the profile gives no date-part evidence to build a timestamp from, and consumers should join to time_hour instead.
time_hour has null_rate 0.0 and every sample_value is a full ISO-8601 instant on the hour (2013-01-01T10:00:00Z), so the VARCHAR is cast to TIMESTAMP.

dep_time and dep_delay (4883 nulls, 0.029388), arr_time (5101 nulls, 0.0307) and arr_delay and air_time (5480 nulls, 0.032981) are retained as nullable; nulls mark non-operated or non-arrived flights and no row is dropped or imputed.
dep_time_missing is derived as true where dep_time is null (4883 of 166158 rows) so consumers can filter non-departed flights deliberately instead of relying on null tests.
tailnum has 1521 nulls (null_rate 0.009154) over 3825 distinct values; the aircraft registration is retained nullable rather than failing the build on a sub-1% gap.

purpose: silver_nyc_flights is the cleaned, typed flight-leg table built from bronze.nyc_flights (166158 rows): one row per scheduled departure leg out of EWR, JFK or LGA, with capture metadata removed, DECIMAL(38,9) measures narrowed to INTEGER, and the hourly timestamp parsed. It feeds downstream on-time-performance and route-volume marts.
usage: Read one row as one scheduled flight leg keyed by time_hour, carrier, flight, origin and sched_dep_time. dep_time, sched_dep_time, arr_time and sched_arr_time are HHMM clock integers (values up to 2400), not minutes, so do not arithmetically subtract them; use dep_delay and arr_delay, which are signed whole minutes and can be negative (min -33 and -86 respectively). Filter dep_time_missing = true out of on-time metrics deliberately, and expect arr_delay and air_time to be null for roughly 3.3% of rows.
limitations: The profile covers only months 1 through 6 of 2013 (month distinct_values 1.0 to 6.0, year a single value 2013.0), so this table is not a full calendar year. Operational outcomes are incomplete: dep_time and dep_delay are null for 2.94% of rows, arr_time for 3.07%, and arr_delay and air_time for 3.30%; those rows are retained, not removed, and no cancellation reason is available in the source. tailnum is null for 0.92% of rows. The declared grain is inferred from column cardinalities rather than measured uniqueness and must be verified before approval; bronze showed duplicate_row_rate 0.0, so no dedupe is applied.
